title: Pipe readv/writev return EINTR despite SA_RESTART
mechanism: Pipe reads and writes wait through wait_events and pause_timeout, which return EINTR; only sys_read/sys_write map EINTR to ERESTARTSYS, while do_sys_readv/do_sys_writev return the raw EINTR, so handle_pending_signal never restarts the vectored calls under SA_RESTART.
contract: signal(7): a blocking read/readv/write/writev on a slow device (such as a pipe) interrupted by a handler installed with SA_RESTART is restarted, not failed with EINTR.
observed: Asterinas returns -1/EINTR from readv on an empty pipe and writev on a full pipe after an SA_RESTART handler runs, while scalar read/write restart in the same boot.

repro.how_to_run: Build repro.c into the initramfs and run it with no arguments in an SMP=2 guest; checks 2 and 4 FAIL with errno=4 on the unfixed kernel while Linux passes 5/5. The regression patch adds process/signal/vectored_io_restart to the process suite.

caveats: The pread64/pwrite64 half is latent (no regular-file EINTR producer; pipes are not seekable). Linux-compatibility defect (spurious EINTR); no security impact beyond that was demonstrated. The GLM CR-2 worktree and its AUTO_TEST wiring were not preserved.
